```{r setup}
library(ghedata)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
```

This article describes the three GitHub tables of the package and shows how the comparison of commits over two years is computed.

## Organisations

```{r}
snapshot_date <- unique(github_organisations$snapshot_date)

counted <- github_organisations |>
  filter(commits_counted)
```

The data was read from GitHub on `r snapshot_date`. Commits are counted in `r nrow(counted)` organisations with `r sum(counted$repos_public) + sum(counted$repos_private)` repositories, of which `r sum(counted$repos_public)` are public and `r sum(counted$repos_private)` are private. Teaching organisations hold one repository per student. They appear in the table with their number of repositories, and their commits are not counted.

```{r}
github_organisations |>
  select(organisation, purpose, commits_counted, repos_public, repos_private) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Commits per month

The table `github_commits` has one row per organisation, visibility and month. The column `commits` counts commits on the default branch of each repository. Merge commits and commits by bots have their own columns and are not part of `commits`. Private repositories are counted and never named.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of commits per month since August 2021 for public and private repositories."
github_commits |>
  summarise(commits = sum(commits), .by = c(month, visibility)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = commits, fill = visibility)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Commits per month", fill = "Repositories") +
  scale_fill_colorblind() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## The last 12 months against the 12 months before

`github_commit_change()` sums the commits of the last 12 complete months in the data and of the 12 months before, and divides the first number by the second.

All organisations, public and private repositories:

```{r}
github_commit_change() |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Public repositories and private repositories of all organisations:

```{r}
bind_rows(
  github_commit_change(visibility = "public"),
  github_commit_change(visibility = "private")
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Private repositories of the Global Health Engineering organisation:

```{r}
github_commit_change(
  organisation = "Global-Health-Engineering",
  visibility = "private"
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Per organisation:

```{r}
unique(github_commits$organisation) |>
  lapply(github_commit_change) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

## Commits with a coding agent

The column `commits_assisted` counts commits whose message names a coding agent in a trailer. The trailer is optional, so the number is a lower bound.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the share of commits per month that carry a trailer of a coding agent."
github_commits |>
  summarise(
    commits = sum(commits),
    commits_assisted = sum(commits_assisted),
    .by = month
  ) |>
  filter(commits > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = commits_assisted / commits)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Share of commits with an agent trailer") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## Public repositories

The table `github_repositories` lists the public repositories. Repositories whose name contains the user name of a person and repositories of student work are left out.

```{r}
github_repositories |>
  count(organisation, repository_type) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
